eventMetadata.context_description: **Forecast models and National Weather Service guidance point to a high in the mid- to upper-90s across Dallas on September 4, 2026, as the remnants of Tropical Depression Edouard dissipate and allow stronger daytime heating under mostly sunny skies.** South to southeast winds of 5–10 mph and dew points in the upper 60s to low 70s support efficient surface warming without significant cloud cover or precipitation after morning hours. This setup aligns with the market’s heavy weighting toward 96–97°F (63.5%), followed by 98–99°F (21.5%), reflecting the consensus range from NWS forecasts of 94–97°F and historical September norms near 93°F. Recent observations from September 3 (94°F max) and the absence of strong upper-level support for extremes keep lower and triple-digit bins at minimal implied probability. Traders appear to be pricing in the latest model runs showing limited variability in peak temperatures before any evening cooling.

title: Highest temperature in Chicago on September 4?
description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Chicago O'Hare Intl Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 4 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=kord

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service guidance and ensemble model consensus point to a peak temperature in the low 90s at Chicago O'Hare, driven by a lingering warm air mass, southerly flow, and ample boundary-layer moisture that supports heat indices near 100°F despite partly cloudy skies. Afternoon clearing and light winds allow surface heating to maximize around 1–3 p.m. CDT before any lake breeze or late-day convection develops. Historical climatology shows September 4 averages near 80°F, so current conditions represent a several-degree positive anomaly; however, modest model spread on exact timing of moisture return and wind shifts keeps implied probabilities tightly clustered between 88–93°F. Updated NWS briefings and hourly observations through early evening remain the key near-term data points for resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Persistent cloud cover, scattered showers, and northeasterly winds are capping daytime heating in Tokyo on September 5, 2026, keeping the maximum temperature tightly clustered around 25–26 °C according to consensus from JMA, GFS-derived models, and other forecasts.** Overcast conditions limit solar insolation while moist onshore flow from the northeast maintains high humidity and suppresses the diurnal temperature range, consistent with current observations of 22–23 °C under rain on September 4. Historical early-September normals near 29 °C are being offset by this unsettled pattern, with afternoon model guidance showing only modest warming to the mid-20s even if partial clearing occurs. Traders assign the highest implied probabilities to 26 °C (41 %) and 25 °C (34 %) because ensemble runs cluster in that narrow band, with lower odds on 27 °C reflecting limited upside potential from any brief breaks in the clouds. Official JMA station readings at the end of the calendar day will resolve the market.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Shanghai Pudong International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=zspd

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

**Forecast model consensus for Shanghai on September 5 points to a daily high near 30–31°C, driving the near-even market split between those two outcomes.** Official guidance from the China Meteorological Administration and global models (GFS, ECMWF) indicate partly cloudy skies with light northeast winds around 10–15 km/h, limited moisture advection, and only modest afternoon convection risk that could trim peak heating by 1°C or allow brief clearing to push it slightly higher. 

Current September 4 conditions—highs of 30–32°C under variable cloud and scattered light rain—provide a baseline for modest day-to-day continuity in this subtropical regime. Urban heat island effects and boundary-layer mixing add small uncertainties, while any earlier or heavier showers would favor the lower end. Updated model runs and the next CMA briefing are the key near-term catalysts that could shift the narrow implied probabilities.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent high-pressure dominance across northern Italy has produced clear skies and light westerly flow over Milan, enabling strong daytime heating ahead of September 5. Ensemble forecasts from GFS and ECMWF guidance indicate afternoon maxima centered on 33–34 °C, with peak solar insolation, low relative humidity near 30 %, and minimal cloud cover supporting the upper end of that range under the current anticyclonic regime. Model runs show limited disagreement on timing of any subtle cooling from the northwest, keeping the distribution tightly clustered. Trader positioning aligns with this consensus, assigning the highest implied probability to 33 °C while pricing modest upside potential if observed readings reach 34–35 °C before sunset. Updated model guidance tomorrow morning will refine the final resolution window.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models from sources including the Finnish Meteorological Institute, Foreca, and Yr.no indicate a high of 17–18°C for Helsinki on September 5, 2026, with limited potential for 19°C.** 

Current conditions on September 4 show highs near 16–18°C under partly cloudy skies with light southwesterly winds and no strong frontal systems approaching. Ensemble guidance supports modest daytime warming to around 18°C amid stable pressure and minimal cloud cover or precipitation, aligning with early-September climatology where average highs hover near 17°C. The market’s heavy weighting toward 18°C (52%) and 17°C (32%) reflects this tight consensus across official forecasts, while the smaller 19°C probability accounts for minor model spread in maximum temperatures. Resolution criteria focus on the official daily maximum recorded at the Helsinki observation site.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Warsaw Chopin Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 6 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=epwa

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Beijing Capital International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 6 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=zbaa

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

**Forecast consensus from official and ensemble models positions 14–16°C as the most probable range for Helsinki’s daily maximum on September 6, 2026.** Multiple sources, including the Finnish Meteorological Institute (Ilmatieteen laitos), Foreca, and Yr.no, currently project a high of 15–16°C under northwesterly flow, while global models such as ECMWF and GFS indicate similar values with limited spread. This aligns with the market’s heavy weighting toward 15°C (42.5%) and 14°C (32.5%), reflecting trader incorporation of these near-term guidance products.

Early-September climatology provides context: the 1991–2020 average high for the date is 17.1°C, so current outlooks sit modestly below normal. Recent observations show Helsinki experiencing daytime maxima of 16–18°C amid a stable post-summer pattern, with no strong warm advection or blocking highs expected to push temperatures higher. Northwesterly winds and modest cloud cover are anticipated to limit diurnal warming, keeping the peak near or slightly under the seasonal norm.

Model uncertainty remains modest at this lead time (roughly 48 hours out), but minor shifts in wind direction or cloud timing could still nudge the maximum by 1–2°C. Traders appear to be pricing the consensus forecast directly, with lower-probability tails (≥17°C or ≤13°C) discounted accordingly until newer runs become available.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent southwest monsoon (habagat) activity and associated cloud cover, thunderstorms, and moderate-to-strong southwesterly winds are the main drivers keeping Manila's September 6 maximum temperature probabilities clustered around 29–31 °C. Official PAGASA guidance and multiple model runs indicate daytime highs of 28–30 °C under mostly overcast skies and frequent showers, limiting solar heating while high humidity and evaporative cooling from rain further cap peaks. Recent intensification of the monsoon has produced widespread rain across Luzon through the weekend, consistent with climatological norms for early September when average highs hover near 29 °C. Trader consensus reflects uncertainty over exact thunderstorm timing and any brief afternoon breaks in cloud cover that could allow isolated readings to reach 31 °C or stay at 28 °C. Updated PAGASA briefings and next model runs will refine these narrow margins ahead of resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent National Weather Service guidance and model consensus point to a highest temperature near 78–79°F at Los Angeles International Airport (LAX) on September 6, 2026, consistent with the market’s leading 45.5% implied probability for that bin.** 

Early September 2026 has featured near-normal highs in the mid-to-upper 70s amid a persistent marine layer and moderate onshore flow. The primary near-term driver is the remnants of Tropical Cyclone Marie, which are expected to increase cloud cover, raise humidity, and bring a 40% chance of showers (mainly afternoon) across Los Angeles County on Sunday. These conditions typically suppress daytime maxima by limiting solar heating while steering patterns keep the region under cooler southwesterly flow. 

Forecasts from the NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard office and ensemble guidance show highs around 79°F at LAX, with coastal zones in the mid-70s and modest inland warming possible but still capped by the marine influence. Historical averages for September 6 sit near 76–77°F, so the current setup reflects only a slight positive departure from climatology. No strong offshore winds or clear-sky high-pressure ridge is present to push readings into the low 80s or higher. 

Traders appear to be weighting the official LAX observation and the stabilizing effect of increased cloud cover and moisture, producing tight clustering around the 76–81°F range. Updated model runs and NWS briefings ahead of the weekend will be the next key data points that could shift these market-implied odds.
